title: OAuth is proved by a real login and its revocation, or it is not called verified
statement: A manual run against a real subscription records, with an isolated Pi configuration directory and a sanitized environment: that after Pi's interactive `/login` exits, a FRESHLY constructed `ModelRuntime` and `ModelRegistry` report the chosen built-in model in `getAvailable()` and return true from `hasConfiguredAuth()`; and that after the stored credential is removed or revoked, the same construction reports the model unavailable. The retained record is sanitized — asserted to contain no token, authorisation header, credential-derived value, username or absolute home path — and is labelled manual, account-bound and single-instance. A fabricated OAuth credential does not satisfy this criterion in any form.
notes: ⚠️ THE SECOND HALF IS NOT OPTIONAL. A model appearing in `getAvailable()` after a login is consistent with the login having worked and equally consistent with it having been available already; only the revocation distinguishes them. ⚠️ THE 'FRESHLY CONSTRUCTED' CLAUSE MATTERS TOO: reusing a runtime built before the login would report a cached snapshot, and 'login UI exited' is not 'login succeeded' — the same rule section 6.2 applies to the exit code. ⚠️ FABRICATION IS EXCLUDED IN THE STATEMENT RATHER THAN IN A NOTE, because it is the cheap way to make this pass and it would prove a storage shape instead of usable authentication. ✅ PASS 2026-09-21 on EVD-0124. One manual, account-bound Windows run with an isolated Pi configuration and a sanitized environment: after a real /login to openai-codex, a freshly constructed ModelRuntime and ModelRegistry reported gpt-5.5 in getAvailable() with hasConfiguredAuth() true, and after the stored credential was removed the same construction reported it unavailable. The record is sanitized and labelled manual, account-bound and single-instance, and no fabricated credential was used. CI run 35644573627 passed the retained test in all four cells. LIMITS: this is registry discovery and its loss. No model request or token refresh was made, removal was local rather than a provider-side revocation, and nothing is inferred for other providers or for Linux.
